subject: Priority lane + burst credits structure and pilot ask
messages:
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: maya@vizibly.ai, logan.ross@vizibly.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Priority lane + burst credits follow-up from demo

Hi Maya / Logan,

Great to meet with you today — appreciate the clarity on Vizibly's month-end burst profile and the need for tight P1 response windows. I promised a short note summarizing a recommended support+SLA structure we can pilot together.

Proposal (high level):
- Priority Lane Plus: 24/7 on-call with 30-minute P1 response (acknowledge) and 4-hour P1 mitigation target.
- Uptime bands: 99.95% base for API endpoints in primary region; regional failover adds 99.9% when activated.
- Burst credits: a pool of "burst minutes" (token-burst cushion) that applies only to scheduled month-end spikes; unused burst rolls into a quarterly buffer (first 2 quarters only).
- Commercial: 12-month committed spend (consumption commit) with a 10% committed discount; 5% additional incentive if commit increases by 2x in year 2.
- Trial: 60-day pilot with capped credits for initial 200M tokens to validate latency/throughput profile.

I've attached a draft SLA and a quick spreadsheet that shows the credit math (how uptime windows map to $ credits). If this looks directionally right I can loop in finance and legal for PO / redline path.

Next steps: can you confirm the 3 things we need to lock for the pilot?
1) Which API endpoints you'd include in the pilot (embedding vs generation).
2) Expected month-end burst magnitude (peak RPS or token rate).
3) Who on your side will handle legal PO?

Thanks — happy to hop on another 30-min call to finalize.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Maya Chen <maya@vizibly.ai>

Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority lane + burst credits follow-up from demo

Thanks Stephanie — good summary. A couple of clarifying questions before we share the pilot endpoints: 

1) Scheduled maintenance: how are planned maintenance windows treated for uptime calculation and credits? We run some model updates that require short rolling restarts across zones.

2) Burst credits: is the burst pool consumed only when latency exceeds X ms or strictly when token usage spikes? We need the mechanism to map to our billing/reporting.

3) P1 definition: 'acknowledge within 30 minutes' is fine, but what does the 4-hour mitigation target mean in practice if an incident requires model failover and customer-side work?

Finally, can you confirm whether Redwood will automatically route to a lower-cost fallback model during platform-wide incidents, or is that something we must build into our app logic? That fallback behavior is important for our CFO review.

Logan (cc) will handle legal intake — he'll share the procurement contact.

—Maya
Maya Chen
CTO, Vizibly
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: maya@vizibly.ai, logan.ross@vizibly.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority lane + burst credits follow-up from demo

Maya — great questions, here's a more concrete breakdown. Priyom and Naomi are on this thread to weigh in on implementation and commercial mechanics.

Planned maintenance:
- Rolling maintenance windows (planned) are excluded from uptime calculations if >72 hours advance notice is given. Short rolling restarts (under 2 hours per region) are considered planned if scheduled in the maintenance calendar; otherwise they count toward uptime. We can add a carveout for quarterly model update windows if you share the cadence.

Burst pool mechanics:
- Burst pool is token-based (not latency-triggered). Consumption occurs when token consumption in a 1-hour sliding window exceeds the agreed threshold. We will expose a meter in Console and surface a webhook so you can reconcile consumption with your billing.
- If you'd prefer latency-triggered switching, we can include a 'fallback policy' in the runtime routing rules (we can auto-route to a lower-capacity / lower-cost model if P99 latency exceeds a threshold for 5 continuous minutes). That requires a short integration to set the fallback model id in your route config.

P1 mitigation:
- Acknowledge (30m) = first response and triage. Mitigation (4h) = either a temporary workaround that restores >80% capacity or a documented rollback/fallback enacted. Full RCA and permanent fix timelines are separate SLA artifacts.

Commercial tweaks we can offer for pilot:
- 60-day pilot with a 100M token free trial + an additional 50M 'burst cushion' credited at start.
- If you sign a 12-month commit within 30 days of pilot end, we can extend a 12% committed discount instead of 10% and include a one-time onboarding credit of $12,000. Naomi, can you confirm this is workable?

Pls see attached "uptime-credit-formula.xlsx" — it shows the exact credit slabs (minor/major/critical) and pro-rata logic.

Thanks,
Stephanie
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: maya@vizibly.ai, logan.ross@vizibly.ai
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority lane + burst credits follow-up from demo

Stephanie / Priyom — finance approves the 12% commit discount (conditional) and the $12k onboarding credit for deals that meet these terms: 12-month commitment, minimum ARR of $150k, and clear PO within 30 days after pilot.

A few knobs and constraints:
- The burst-credit pool is accounted as a pre-burned credit on the invoice for the pilot period; any overage beyond the cushion will be invoiced at standard usage rates.
- Planned maintenance carveouts need to be logged in the Console maintenance calendar 72 hours prior; exceptions require CS approval.
- For renewals we can tier in an additional 2% rebate if usage grows 2x year-over-year.

I've attached the onboarding credit terms doc. If legal redlines are required, route them through Logan and we will start a DocuSign addendum for the pilot terms.

—Naomi

From: Logan Ross <logan.ross@vizibly.ai>

Thanks — this is helpful and close to what procurement needs. Couple of quick asks before we route to legal: 

1) Can you share a sample invoice that shows how the burst pre-credit and any overage would appear? We want to show CFO the worst-case billing scenario.
2) We need an explicit numeric formula for outage credits (example: X% credit for Y minutes by severity). The spreadsheet is useful but procurement prefers the formula baked into the SLA doc.

One last ask: will Redwood enable automatic fallback routing to a lower-cost model as an opt-in for the pilot? If so, can you include the config steps in a short implementation appendix so our infra team can test it during the pilot?

If you can provide those items by EOD Wednesday, we'll kick legal the next day.

Thanks,
